name: Tobiasz Wierzbicki
headline: Senior Application Security Engineer
summary: Application security engineer with twelve years in secure software delivery, the last six leading a small AppSec team. I embed threat modelling and code review into how product squads work, and I care more about fixing root causes than about long vulnerability reports. Outside work I run a local meetup on secure development and write short internal guides for new engineers.

bullets: Built a security champions network of 28 developers; critical findings reaching production fell by 61% in two years.
Introduced threat modelling workshops for every new payment feature, reviewing roughly 40 designs per year.
Tuned Semgrep rules and static analysis gates in the build pipeline, cutting false positives from 70% to under 20%.
Ran the private bug bounty programme, triaging 300+ reports and agreeing remediation SLAs with engineering leads.

Published a developer-friendly secure coding handbook with worked Java and Go examples, now part of every engineer's onboarding. Partnered with legal and compliance to map PCI requirements onto concrete engineering tasks.
Performed manual code reviews of Java services handling authentication and session management.
Ran quarterly penetration tests against internal web apps and wrote clear remediation guidance for developers.
Rolled out a central secrets vault and retired hard-coded credentials across 60 repositories.
Reported findings in the team backlog rather than PDFs, which doubled the fix rate within one sprint.
Evaluated three static analysis products and recommended the one that best fitted our monorepo.
Developed Java back-end services for logistics customers.
Fixed injection and access-control flaws found in customer audits and learned secure coding on the job.
Earned a reputation for explaining injection attacks with live demos during lunch sessions.

name: Chidinma Okonkwo-Eze
headline: Cloud Security Engineer
summary: Cloud security engineer focused on AWS and Azure guardrails. I turn compliance requirements into automated, preventive controls and help engineering teams ship safely without waiting on a manual review. Previously a SOC analyst, so I know what detection looks like from the receiving end. I mentor two junior colleagues and speak at community security meetups about cloud misconfigurations.

bullets: Designed service control policies and account guardrails across 120 AWS accounts, blocking public storage by default.
Added Checkov scanning of CloudFormation templates to the delivery pipelines, catching misconfigurations before deployment.
Reduced mean time to remediate high-severity cloud findings from 19 days to 4.
Wrote an IAM review playbook adopted by all platform squads.

Automated evidence collection for ISO 27001 audits, saving the compliance team roughly 15 days of work each cycle. Partnered with finance to tag and review accounts, uncovering several forgotten test environments with open access.
Monitored alerts in Splunk, investigated incidents and escalated confirmed compromises.
Built detection rules for suspicious API key use that raised the true-positive rate noticeably.
Contributed to the incident response runbooks and ran tabletop exercises twice a year.
Tuned noisy alerts by adding context from asset inventory, which let the team focus on real incidents.
Presented a lessons-learned review of a credential leak to senior management.
First-line support for 400 users, account lifecycle and endpoint hygiene.
Moved into security after automating the leaver process in Python.
Learned scripting and basic networking, which later became the foundation for cloud work.

name: Rúben Taveirinha
headline: Engenheiro de Segurança Aplicacional
summary: Engenheiro de segurança com nove anos de experiência em aplicações web e APIs. Trabalho lado a lado com as equipas de desenvolvimento para encontrar vulnerabilidades cedo, explicar o risco em linguagem simples e acompanhar a correção até ao fim. Gosto de partilhar o que aprendo em conferências e comunidades de segurança em Portugal.

bullets: Realizo testes de intrusão a portais de clientes e APIs de parceiros, com cerca de 25 relatórios por ano.
Criei uma lista de verificação de segurança para revisões de código que passou a ser usada por seis equipas.
Integrei a análise estática no processo de entrega e reduzi para metade as vulnerabilidades repetidas.
Dou formações trimestrais a programadores sobre injeção, controlo de acessos e gestão de sessões.

Defini métricas simples de risco, como tempo médio de correção por gravidade, e apresento-as todos os meses à direção. Colaborei com o apoio ao cliente para identificar padrões de fraude nas contas online.
Auditei aplicações web de clientes da banca e da energia e recomendei correções priorizadas.
Apoiei a preparação para auditorias de conformidade com o RGPD.
Desenvolvi ferramentas internas em Python para automatizar a recolha de evidências.
Participei em dezenas de reuniões de apresentação de resultados e treinei jovens consultores em testes web.
Criei modelos de relatório reutilizáveis que reduziram o tempo de escrita em cerca de 30%.
Desenvolvimento de funcionalidades em C# e correção de defeitos em aplicações internas.
Aprendi com os colegas mais velhos as boas práticas de validação de dados de entrada e tratamento de erros.
Participei em revisões de arquitetura e propus validações de entrada mais rigorosas nos formulários públicos da empresa.

name: Siobhán Ní Bhriain
headline: Security Operations Analyst

Calm under pressure, I write clear handover notes and enjoy explaining incidents to non-technical colleagues.

bullets: Triage around 60 alerts per shift in Microsoft Sentinel and escalate genuine incidents with clear timelines.
Wrote 15 KQL detection rules for credential stuffing and impossible-travel sign-ins.
Analysed reported phishing emails and cut average response time to 25 minutes.
Shadow senior analysts during incident calls and prepare post-incident summaries for customers.

Helped review firewall logs and maintain the vulnerability scan schedule.
Documented the account recovery process and flagged two weaknesses to the IT manager.

Set up automatic updates and basic backups, and wrote a one-page security guide for volunteers.

name: Lukas Hartmannsdorf
headline: Principal Penetration Tester

Coach junior testers and review every report before it reaches the client.

headline: Analista de Negócio
summary: Analista de negócio com cinco anos de experiência em turismo e hotelaria. Gosto de perceber como as pessoas trabalham, documentar processos e propor melhorias simples que a equipa realmente adota. Aprendo depressa, comunico com clareza e tenho especial gosto por ajudar equipas não técnicas a trabalhar com tecnologia. Estou sempre disponível para aprender novas ferramentas e processos.

bullets: Levanto requisitos para o novo sistema de reservas usado por 14 unidades hoteleiras.
Mapeei os processos de check-in e faturação e identifiquei três passos duplicados que foram eliminados.
Construí relatórios em Power BI sobre ocupação e receita por quarto.
Coordeno os testes de aceitação com a receção e a contabilidade.
Preparei materiais de formação e manuais para a equipa de receção em seis línguas. Faço a ponte entre os fornecedores de software e as equipas operacionais dos hotéis.
Analisei dados de vendas e preparei relatórios mensais para a direção.
Documentei requisitos para melhorias no site de reservas.
Criei um modelo de análise de custos por canal de venda, usado em reuniões comerciais.
Apresentei propostas de melhoria diretamente à administração.
Apoio administrativo e recolha de dados de clientes.
Aprendi a trabalhar com folhas de cálculo complexas e a validar dados antes de os partilhar.
Organizei ficheiros de reservas e ajudei na resposta a pedidos de clientes em português e inglês.
Aprendi a trabalhar com sistemas de reservas e a dar apoio a utilizadores em momentos de pressão.

name: Dariusz Nowaczyk
headline: Business Analyst
summary: Business analyst with six years in retail and e-commerce. I gather requirements, map processes and report on sales performance. I work with technical teams every day and keep up with the vocabulary, including Kubernetes, Terraform and CI/CD, although I have no hands-on experience with them. Outside work I volunteer with a local board-game club and enjoy hiking. I am organised, detail-oriented and good at explaining numbers.
skills: Buzzwords from job ads: Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD, DevOps, AWS, microservices, cloud-native

bullets: Gather and document requirements for pricing, promotions and loyalty features.
Built Tableau dashboards on sales and basket size used in weekly management meetings.
Coordinate user acceptance testing with store operations and the e-commerce team.
Estimate benefits for business cases; the loyalty redesign was projected at 3% uplift in repeat purchases.
Work closely with the IT team on release scheduling and write test scenarios for each new version. Maintain a glossary of business terms and system names shared with new colleagues.
Wrote user stories for the seller portal and refined backlog items with the product owner.
Prepared monthly Excel reports on returns and delivery delays.
Presented findings from customer survey analysis to the marketplace management team.
Helped negotiate service levels with two logistics partners.
Maintained product data and supported campaign planning.
Learned about marketplace operations and seller onboarding.
Prepared promotional price files and checked them against catalogue data before every campaign launch.
Trained store staff on the new promotion tool and collected feedback for improvements.
Learned to build lookup tables and validate data in spreadsheets.

name: Fiona Gallagher-Moran
headline: Lead Business Analyst
summary: Lead business analyst with fourteen years of experience in public sector and utilities programmes. I specialise in complex stakeholder environments, benefits tracking and requirements that survive procurement and audit. I coach teams in plain-English documentation and believe good analysis should shorten meetings, not lengthen them. I enjoy complex programmes where careful analysis makes a difference.

bullets: Lead a team of four analysts on a customer billing replacement worth £18m.
Wrote the requirements and evaluation criteria used to select the supplier among six bidders.
Track benefits across three workstreams and report monthly to the programme board.
Facilitate workshops with 12 departments to settle conflicting requirements.

Chair a monthly community of practice for analysts across three departments. Review all programme documents before they go to the board, checking for gaps and ambiguity. Escalate risks early with options and costs.
Redesigned citizen service processes, reducing average case time by 27%.
Produced traceability matrices for audit.
Mentored new analysts.
Supported three audits without major findings thanks to consistent traceability.
Facilitated lessons-learned sessions after major releases.
Documented requirements for a housing repairs system.
Learned the basics of public sector funding and grant reporting.
Ran stakeholder interviews and wrote the functional specification used by the supplier to build the system.
Prepared monthly progress reports for the housing board.
Supported tenant consultation events and summarised their feedback for decision makers.

name: Emeka Onwuachi
headline: Business Analyst, Data
summary: Business analyst working at the border between business and data. Four years in telecoms, specialising in reporting needs, KPIs and data quality. I translate what managers say they want into what the data can really show. I am studying for a data analytics certificate and want to grow into a data product role. I document carefully and challenge assumptions politely.

bullets: Define and document 60 KPIs for the commercial team and agree calculation rules with finance.
Wrote SQL to reconcile billing and usage data, finding about 2% revenue leakage.
Built Power BI reports for regional sales managers in four states.
Gather requirements for a new customer self-service portal.

Created a data dictionary and data quality checklist adopted by the BI team. Meet weekly with regional managers to refine dashboard requirements. Present data findings to the commercial director each quarter with clear recommendations and caveats.
Documented processes and requirements for a mobile money project.
Supported UAT cycles and logged defects.
Helped train 50 field agents on the new mobile money app.
Wrote test scripts and tracked defects to closure with developers.
Mapped the mobile money onboarding journey and proposed three changes that reduced rejected registrations.
Reconciled daily transaction reports and flagged inconsistencies to the supervisor.
Learned SQL and Excel automation to replace manual report preparation.
Prepared training notes for new clerks on reporting standards.
